paper.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale

result.summary: 本文提出 Vision Transformer（ViT），将图像切分为固定大小的图像块，线性嵌入后加上位置嵌入，直接送入标准 Transformer 编码器进行图像分类 [S1.p3][S3.F1]。作者在 ImageNet、ImageNet-21k 和 JFT-300M 等不同规模数据集上预训练，并迁移到多个图像识别基准 [S4.SS1.p1]。结果显示，大规模预训练下 ViT 在多个基准上达到或超过当时最优卷积网络，且预训练计算资源更少 [S1.p5][S4.T2]。作者认为，这一简单且可扩展的策略在配合大规模预训练时效果出人意料地好 [S5.p1]。

research_question.text: 论文要解决的问题是：在计算机视觉中，卷积架构仍占主导，能否不依赖 CNN，而将标准 Transformer 直接应用于图像分类 [S1.p2][S1.p3]。其动机来自 Transformer 在 NLP 中的成功与可扩展性，作者希望以尽可能少的修改把标准 Transformer 直接用于图像 [S1.p1][S1.p3]。

evidence.quote: Self-attention-based architectures, in particular Transformers, have become the model of choice in natural language processing (NLP).
In computer vision, however, convolutional architectures remain dominant.
Inspired by the Transformer scaling successes in NLP, we experiment with applying a standard Transformer directly to images, with the fewest possible modifications.

method.text: 方法上，作者尽量遵循原始 Transformer 的设计，将图像切分为固定大小的图像块，对每个图像块做线性嵌入并加入位置嵌入，再把得到的向量序列送入标准 Transformer 编码器 [S3.F1][S3.p1]。为进行分类，作者在序列中加入一个可学习的分类 token，并将其输出作为图像表示 [S3.F1][S3.SS1.p2]。此外，作者还提出混合架构，即输入序列可以由 CNN 特征图构成 [S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1]。

evidence.quote: We split an image into fixed-size patches, linearly embed each of them, add position embeddings, and feed the resulting sequence of vectors to a standard Transformer encoder.
In model design we follow the original Transformer as closely as possible.
Similar to BERT’s [class] token, we prepend a learnable embedding to the sequence of embedded patches
As an alternative to raw image patches, the input sequence can be formed from feature maps of a CNN.

experiments.text: 实验在 ILSVRC-2012 ImageNet（1k 类、1.3M 图像）、ImageNet-21k（21k 类、14M 图像）和 JFT（18k 类、303M 高分辨率图像）上预训练，并迁移到 ImageNet、CIFAR-10/100、Oxford-IIIT Pets、Oxford Flowers-102 以及 19 任务的 VTAB 分类套件 [S4.SS1.p1][S4.SS1.p2]。基线 CNN 使用将 Batch Normalization 替换为 Group Normalization 的 ResNet（BiT），混合模型则把中间特征图以 1 像素的 patch 送入 ViT [S4.SS1.p4]。评价指标包括微调精度和 few-shot 精度 [S4.SS1.p6]。

evidence.quote: we use the ILSVRC-2012 ImageNet dataset with 1k classes and 1.3M images
its superset ImageNet-21k with 21k classes and 14M images, and JFT with 18k classes and 303M high-resolution images
We also evaluate on the 19-task VTAB classification suite.
For the baseline CNNs, we use ResNet, but replace the Batch Normalization layers with Group Normalization
We report results on downstream datasets either through few-shot or fine-tuning accuracy.

findings.text: 在 JFT-300M 上预训练的 ViT 在所有数据集上优于基于 ResNet 的基线，同时预训练计算资源显著更少 [S4.T2]。最佳模型在 ImageNet 上达到 88.55%、ImageNet-ReaL 上 90.72%、CIFAR-100 上 94.55%、VTAB 19 任务上 77.63% 的精度 [S1.p5]。ViT-H/14 在 VTAB 的 Natural 和 Structured 任务上超过 BiT-R152x4 等方法，而在 Specialized 上前两名模型表现相近 [S4.SS2.p3]。数据规模方面，在最小数据集 ImageNet 上 ViT-Large 不如 ViT-Base，在 ImageNet-21k 上两者相近，只有 JFT-300M 才体现出更大模型的全部优势 [S4.SS3.p2]。

evidence.quote: Vision Transformer models pre-trained on the JFT-300M dataset outperform ResNet-based baselines on all datasets, while taking substantially less computational resources to pre-train.
the best model reaches the accuracy of $88.55\%$ on ImageNet, $90.72\%$ on ImageNet-ReaL, $94.55\%$ on CIFAR-100, and $77.63\%$ on the VTAB suite of 19 tasks.
ViT-H/14 outperforms BiT-R152x4, and other methods, on the Natural and Structured tasks.
On the Specialized the performance of the top two models is similar.
When pre-trained on the smallest dataset, ImageNet, ViT-Large models underperform compared to ViT-Base models
Only with JFT-300M, do we see the full benefit of larger models.

limitations.text: 作者指出，仍有许多挑战：一是将 ViT 应用于检测、分割等其他计算机视觉任务 [S5.p2]；二是继续探索自监督预训练方法，初步实验显示自监督预训练有提升，但与大规模监督预训练之间仍有较大差距 [S5.p2]。此外，自监督的 masked patch prediction 下 ViT-B/16 在 ImageNet 上达到 79.9%，比从头训练提升 2%，但仍落后监督预训练 4% [S4.SS6.p1]。

evidence.quote: One is to apply ViT to other computer vision tasks, such as detection and segmentation.
Our initial experiments show improvement from self-supervised pre-training, but there is still large gap between self-supervised and large-scale supervised pre-training.
our smaller ViT-B/16 model achieves 79.9% accuracy on ImageNet, a significant improvement of 2% to training from scratch, but still 4% behind supervised pre-training.
